title: Self-Checking Weekend Practice Pack
whatYouGet: A weekend pack with attempt-first sequencing, delayed hints, external checks and a Monday error reflection.
howToUse: Set the weekend scope and time budget, check the pack, then instruct students to open links only after attempting.
effectiveUsage: 1. Define a realistic weekend scope and total time.
2. Review questions, delayed hints and all answer checks.
3. Share the attempt-first instructions with students and parents.
4. Use Monday reflections to choose the next practice branch.
commonFix: If wrong, reply with: "Shorten the workload, hide final answers until after the attempt and rebuild every check link from its exact fallback."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as an attempt-first homework designer and self-check workflow editor.

CONTEXT: Students in [CLASS] need a [TOTAL MINUTES]-minute weekend pack on [SKILL MIX] with responsible self-checking.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [CLASS]
- [SKILL MIX]
- [TOTAL MINUTES]
- [QUESTION COUNT]
- [HINT POLICY]
- [PARENT MESSAGE]
- [MONDAY FOLLOW-UP]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [WOLFRAMALPHA] Whitelist: https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i={ENCODED_PLAIN_CALCULATOR_QUERY}. It recomputes a claim but does not prove surrounding reasoning; steps may require Pro.
- [SYMBOLAB] Whitelist: https://www.symbolab.com/solver?query={ENCODED_PLAIN_CALCULATOR_QUERY}. Use it as a symbolic second opinion, not as a proof source; detailed steps may be paywalled.
- [KHAN_ACADEMY] Whitelist: https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Use search only; never invent opaque Khan topic or exercise paths.

DO THIS:
1. Allocate time across retrieval, core practice, one challenge and reflection.
2. Write original questions in a deliberate order and solve every one.
3. Place graduated hints after a clear attempt boundary and keep final answers later still.
4. Create WolframAlpha or Symbolab check links only for computable claims with exact fallbacks.
5. Use Khan search links for optional extra practice, never guessed topic paths.
6. Add a Monday error-log prompt that asks for the first difficult step rather than a score only.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Build a self-check link for solving x^2-5x+6=0 after the attempt.
Expected result or check target: The student can inspect roots 2 and 3, then record the first step that caused difficulty.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=solve%20x%5E2-5x%2B6%3D0
(paste-fallback: solve x^2-5x+6=0)
Encoding note: The link payload decodes exactly to the fallback and is separate from any invented quiz or topic route.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Weekend Plan — skill and time allocation
2. Attempt Pack — original questions before hints
3. Hint Ladder — delayed support without answer leakage
4. Self-Check Routes — exact external links and fallbacks
5. Monday Reflection — first difficult step and next action

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Never invent Wolfram Problem Generator quiz slugs or Khan topic URLs.
- Use Wolfram quizzes only from supplied whitelist rows and Khan only through search URLs.
- Label generated questions ORIGINAL PRACTICE, not official or PYQ material.
- External checks must be labelled check this yourself and opened only after an attempt.
- Keep the total workload inside [TOTAL MINUTES] and preserve an offline route.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
- Never output a desmos.com URL with parameters, a mathsolver.microsoft.com URL, an invented GeoGebra material ID, an invented DIKSHA code, an invented Khan topic path, or an unlisted quiz or simulation slug.
- Never describe an AI answer as verified. Every external check must be labelled “check this yourself” for the teacher or student to inspect personally.
- Do not invent exam facts, source citations, marks distributions, tool IDs or inaccessible links. Separate mathematical proof from computational checking.

1. You may output clickable links ONLY to: wolframalpha.com/input?i= · symbolab.com/solver?query= ·

   artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_ · khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query= ·
   overleaf.com/docs?encoded_snip= · latex.codecogs.com/png.image? · docs.google.com/forms/...viewform?usp=pp_url
   (Forms only with entry.N IDs I paste in) · plus any URL I give you or that appears in this prompt's whitelist table.

title: Turn Raw Marks Into Re-Teach Priorities

howToUse: Paste the test export, question maxima, and topic map; review the error queue before using the ranked re-teach plan.

2. Remove names if stable anonymous IDs are available.

4. Pair the ranking with teacher observation before re-teaching.
commonFix: If priorities look implausible, ask for the cleaned denominator table and check whether blanks, absences, and zero marks were separated.

title: Calculate Question Difficulty From Response Rows
whatYouGet: A question-wise facility table that distinguishes correct, partial, wrong, blank, and absent responses.
howToUse: Supply item-level marks and maxima, then confirm the denominator policy before pasting formulas into Sheets.
effectiveUsage: 1. Use one response row per learner and item.

commonFix: If every item appears too easy or hard, ask the analysis to print numerator and denominator columns beside each index.

title: Compare Top and Bottom Group Discrimination
whatYouGet: An auditable upper-lower group discrimination table with tie handling and small-sample warnings.
howToUse: Paste total scores and item outcomes, specify group size and tie policy, then inspect group membership before reading indices.
effectiveUsage: 1. Use anonymous stable IDs.
2. State the upper and lower group rule.
3. Freeze tie handling before computing.
4. Review negative indices against the key and item wording.
commonFix: If group membership changes unexpectedly, request the sorted score CSV with rank, tie flag, and inclusion reason.

whatYouGet: A rectangular student-topic matrix, conditional-formatting plan, and error queue built from mapped assessment rows.
howToUse: Provide response data and a teacher-approved question-topic map, then paste the generated matrix and formulas into Sheets.
